verses.zh: 论异象谷的默示：有甚么事使你这满城的人都上房顶呢？
verses.en: This is an oracle[NOTE:1] about the Valley of Vision:[NOTE:2] What is the reason[NOTE:3] that all of you go up to the rooftops?
notes: See note at Isa 13:1.

The following message pertains to Jerusalem. The significance of referring to the city as the Valley of Vision is uncertain. Perhaps the Hinnom Valley is in view, but why it is associated with a prophetic revelatory “vision” is not entirely clear. Maybe the Hinnom Valley is called this because the destruction that will take place there is the focal point of this prophetic message (see v. 5).
Heb “What to you, then?”

verses.zh: 你这满处呐喊、大有喧哗的城，欢乐的邑啊，你中间被杀的并不是被刀杀，也不是因打仗死亡。
verses.en: The noisy city is full of raucous sounds;the town is filled with revelry.[NOTE:1] Your slain were not cut down by the sword;they did not die in battle.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “the boisterous town.” The phrase is parallel to “the noisy city” in the preceding line.
Apparently they died from starvation during the siege that preceded the final conquest of the city. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:409.

verses.zh: 你所有的官长一同逃跑，都为弓箭手所捆绑。你中间一切被找到的都一同被捆绑；他们本是逃往远方的。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] All your leaders ran away together—they fled to a distant place;all your refugees[NOTE:2] were captured together—they were captured without a single arrow being shot.[NOTE:3]
notes: Verse 3 reads literally, “All your leaders ran away; apart from a bow they were captured; all your found ones were captured together; to a distant place they fled.” J. N. Oswalt (Isaiah [NICOT], 1:403, n. 3) suggests that the lines of the verse are arranged chiastically; lines 1 and 4 go together, while lines 2 and 3 are parallel. To translate the lines in the order they appear in the Hebrew text is misleading to the English reader, who is likely unfamiliar with, or at least insensitive to, chiastic parallelism. Consequently, the main translation arranges the lines as follows: line 1 (Hebrew) = line 1 (in translation); line 2 (Hebrew) = line 4 (in translation); line 3 (Hebrew) = line 3 (in translation); line 4 (Hebrew) = line 2 (in translation).

Heb “all your found ones.” To achieve tighter parallelism (see “your leaders”) some prefer to emend the form to אַמִּיצַיִךְ (ʾammitsayikh, “your strong ones”) or to נֶאֱמָצַיִךְ (neʾematsayikh, “your strengthened ones”).
Heb “apart from [i.e., without] a bow they were captured”; cf. NAB, NRSV “without the use of a bow.”

verses.zh: 所以我说：你们转眼不看我，我要痛哭。不要因我众民（原文是民女）的毁灭，就竭力安慰我。
verses.en: So I say:“Don’t look at me![NOTE:1] I am weeping bitterly.Don’t try[NOTE:2] to console meconcerning the destruction of my defenseless people.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “look away from me” (so KJV, ASV, NRSV).
Heb “don’t hurry” (so NCV).
Heb “the daughter of my people.” “Daughter” is here used metaphorically to express the speaker’s emotional attachment to his people, as well as their vulnerability and weakness.

verses.zh: 因为主―万军之耶和华使「异象谷」有溃乱、践踏、烦扰的日子。城被攻破，哀声达到山间。
verses.en: For the Sovereign[NOTE:1] Lord of Heaven’s Armieshas planned a day of panic, defeat, and confusion.[NOTE:2] In the Valley of Vision[NOTE:3] people shout[NOTE:4] and cry out to the hill.[NOTE:5]
notes: The Hebrew term translated “Sovereign” here and in vv. 12, 14, 15 is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay).
Heb “For [there is] a day of panic, and trampling, and confusion for the master, the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”].”
The traditional accentuation of the Hebrew text suggests that this phrase goes with what precedes.

The precise meaning of this statement is unclear. Some take קִר (qir) as “wall” and interpret the verb to mean “tear down.” However, tighter parallelism (note the reference to crying for help in the next line) is achieved if one takes both the verb and noun from a root, attested in Ugaritic and Arabic, meaning “make a sound.” See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:404, n. 5.
Perhaps “the hill” refers to the temple mount.

verses.zh: 以拦带着箭袋，还有坐战车的和马兵；吉珥揭开盾牌。
verses.en: The Elamites picked up the quiverand came with chariots and horsemen;[NOTE:1] the men of Kir[NOTE:2] prepared[NOTE:3] the shield.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “[with] the chariots of men, horsemen.”
A distant region in the direction of Mesopotamia; see Amos 1:5; 9:7.
Heb “Kir uncovers” (so NAB, NIV).

The Elamites and men of Kir may here symbolize a fierce army from a distant land. If this oracle anticipates a Babylonian conquest of the city (see 39:5-7), then the Elamites and men of Kir are perhaps viewed here as mercenaries in the Babylonian army. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:410.

verses.zh: 你嘉美的谷遍满战车，也有马兵在城门前排列。
verses.en: Your very best valleys were full of chariots;[NOTE:1] horsemen confidently took their positions[NOTE:2] at the gate.
notes: The verb that introduces this verse serves as a discourse particle and is untranslated; see note on “in the future” in 2:2.
Heb “taking a stand, take their stand.” The infinitive absolute emphasizes the following finite verb. The translation attempts to bring out this emphasis with the adverb “confidently.”

verses.zh: 他去掉犹大的遮盖。那日，你就仰望林库内的军器。
verses.en: They[NOTE:1] removed the defenses[NOTE:2] of Judah.At that time[NOTE:3] you lookedfor the weapons in the House of the Forest.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “he,” i.e., the enemy invader. NASB, by its capitalization of the pronoun, takes this to refer to the Lord.
Heb “covering.”
Heb “in that day” (so KJV); likewise at the beginning of v. 12.
Perhaps this refers to a royal armory, or to Solomon’s “House of the Forest of Lebanon,” where weapons may have been kept (see 1 Kgs 10:16-17).

verses.zh: 你们看见大卫城的破口很多，便聚积下池的水，
verses.en: You saw the many breaksin the walls of the City of David;[NOTE:1] you stored up water in the lower pool.
notes: Heb “the breaks of the City of David, you saw that they were many.”

verses.zh: 又数点耶路撒冷的房屋，将房屋拆毁，修补城墙，
verses.en: You counted the houses in Jerusalem[NOTE:1] and demolished houses so you could have material to reinforce the wall.[NOTE:2]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “you demolished the houses to fortify the wall.”

verses.zh: 又在两道城墙中间挖一个聚水池可盛旧池的水，却不仰望做这事的主，也不顾念从古定这事的。
verses.en: You made a reservoir between the two wallsfor the water of the old pool—but you did not trust in[NOTE:1] the one who made it;[NOTE:2] you did not depend on[NOTE:3] the one who formed it long ago.
notes: Heb “look at”; NAB, NRSV “did not look to.”

The antecedent of the third feminine singular suffix here and in the next line is unclear. The closest feminine noun is “pool” in the first half of the verse. Perhaps this “old pool” symbolizes the entire city, which had prospered because of God’s provision and protection through the years.
Heb “did not see.”

verses.zh: 当那日，主―万军之耶和华叫人哭泣哀号，头上光秃，身披麻布。
verses.en: At that time the Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies called for weeping and mourning,for shaved heads and sackcloth.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for baldness and the wearing of sackcloth.” See the note at 15:2.

verses.zh: 谁知，人倒欢喜快乐，宰牛杀羊，吃肉喝酒，说：我们吃喝吧！因为明天要死了。
verses.en: But look, there is outright celebration![NOTE:1] You say, “Kill the ox and slaughter the sheep,eat meat and drink wine.Eat and drink, for tomorrow we die!”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “happiness and joy.”

The prophet here quotes what the fatalistic people are saying. The introductory “you say” is supplied in the translation for clarification; the concluding verb “we die” makes it clear the people are speaking. The six verbs translated as imperatives are actually infinitives absolute, functioning here as finite verbs.

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华亲自默示我说：这罪孽直到你们死，断不得赦免！这是主―万军之耶和华说的。
verses.en: The Lord of Heaven’s Armies told me this:[NOTE:1] “Certainly this sin will not be forgiven as long as you live,”[NOTE:2] says the Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies.
notes: Heb “it was revealed in my ears [by?] the Lord of Heaven’s Armies [traditionally, “the Lord of hosts”].”

Heb “Certainly this sin will not be atoned for until you die.” This does not imply that their death will bring atonement; rather it emphasizes that their sin is unpardonable. The statement has the form of an oath.

verses.zh: 主―万军之耶和华这样说：「你去见掌银库的，就是家宰舍伯那，对他说：
verses.en: This is what the Sovereign Lord of Heaven’s Armies says:“Go visit this administrator, Shebna, who supervises the palace,[NOTE:1] and tell him:[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “who is over the house” (so ASV); NASB “who is in charge of the royal household.”
The words “and tell him” are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 『你在这里做甚么呢？有甚么人竟在这里凿坟墓，就是在高处为自己凿坟墓，在磐石中为自己凿出安身之所？
verses.en: ‘What right do you have to be here? What relatives do you have buried here?[NOTE:1] Why[NOTE:2] do you chisel out a tomb for yourself here?He chisels out his burial site in an elevated place,he carves out his tomb on a cliff.
notes: Heb “What to you here? And who to you here?” The point of the second question is not entirely clear. The interpretation reflected in the translation is based on the following context, which suggests that Shebna has no right to think of himself so highly and arrange such an extravagant burial place for himself.
Heb “that you chisel out.”

verses.zh: 看哪，耶和华必像大有力的人，将你紧紧缠裹，竭力抛去。
verses.en: Look, the Lord will throw you far away,[NOTE:1] you mere man![NOTE:2] He will wrap you up tightly.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “will throw you with a throwing.”
Heb “O man” (so NASB); NAB “mortal man”; NRSV “my fellow.”
Heb “and the one who wraps you [will] wrap.”

verses.zh: 他必将你滚成一团，抛在宽阔之地，好像抛球一样。你这主人家的羞辱，必在那里坐你荣耀的车，也必在那里死亡。
verses.en: He will wind you up tightly into a balland throw you into a wide, open land.[NOTE:1] There you will die,and there with you will be your impressive chariots,[NOTE:2] which bring disgrace to the house of your master.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and he will tightly [or “surely”] wind you [with] winding like a ball, to a land broad of hands [i.e., “sides”].”
Heb “and there the chariots of your splendor.”
Apparently the reference to chariots alludes to Shebna’s excessive pride, which in turn brings disgrace to the royal family.

verses.zh: 我必赶逐你离开官职；你必从你的原位撤下。』
verses.en: I will remove you from[NOTE:1] your office;you will be thrown down[NOTE:2] from your position.
notes: Heb “I will push you away from.”

Heb “he will throw you down.” The shift from the first to third person is peculiar and abrupt, but certainly not unprecedented in Hebrew poetry. See GKC 462 §144.p. The third person may be indefinite (“one will throw you down”), in which case the passive translation is justified.

verses.zh: 「到那日，我必召我仆人希勒家的儿子以利亚敬来，
verses.en: “‘At that time[NOTE:1] I will summon my servant Eliakim, son of Hilkiah.
notes: Or “in that day.” The verb that introduces this verse serves as a discourse particle and is untranslated; see note on “in the future” in 2:2.

verses.zh: 将你的外袍给他穿上，将你的腰带给他系紧，将你的政权交在他手中。他必作耶路撒冷居民和犹大家的父。
verses.en: I will put your robe on him, tie your belt around him, and transfer your authority to him.[NOTE:1] He will become a protector of[NOTE:2] the residents of Jerusalem and of the people[NOTE:3] of Judah.
notes: Heb “and your dominion I will place in his hand.”

Heb “a father to.” The Hebrew term אָב (ʾav, “father”) is here used metaphorically of one who protects and supports those under his care and authority, like a father does his family. For another example of this metaphorical use of the word, see Job 29:16.
Heb “house.”

verses.zh: 我必将大卫家的钥匙放在他肩头上。他开，无人能关；他关，无人能开。
verses.en: I will place the key[NOTE:1] to the house of David on his shoulder. When he opens the door, no one can close it; when he closes the door, no one can open it.
notes: This may refer to a literal insignia worn by the chief administrator. Even so, it would still symbolize the administrator’s authority to grant or exclude access to the king. See J. N. Oswalt, Isaiah (NICOT), 1:422.

verses.zh: 我必将他安稳，像钉子钉在坚固处；他必作为他父家荣耀的宝座。
verses.en: I will fasten him like a peg into a solid place;[NOTE:1] he will bring honor and respect to his father’s family.[NOTE:2]
notes: The metaphor depicts how secure his position will be.
Heb “and he will become a glorious throne for the house of his father.”

verses.zh: 他父家所有的荣耀，连儿女带子孙，都挂在他身上，好像一切小器皿，从杯子到酒瓶挂上一样。
verses.en: His father’s family will gain increasing prominence because of him,[NOTE:1] including the offspring and the offshoots.[NOTE:2] All the small containers, including the bowls and all the jars, will hang from this peg.’[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “and all the glory of the house of his father they will hang on him.” The Lord returns to the peg metaphor of v. 23a. Eliakim’s secure position of honor will bring benefits and jobs to many others in the family.
The precise meaning and derivation of this word are uncertain. Cf. KJV, ASV, NRSV “the issue”; CEV “relatives.”
Heb “all the small vessels, from the vessels that are bowls to all the vessels that are jars.” The picture is that of a single peg holding the weight of all kinds of containers hung from it.

verses.zh: 万军之耶和华说：当那日，钉在坚固处的钉子必压斜，被砍断落地；挂在其上的重担必被剪断。因为这是耶和华说的。」
verses.en: “At that time,”[NOTE:1] says the Lord of Heaven’s Armies, “the peg fastened into a solid place will come loose. It will be cut off and fall, and the load hanging on it will be cut off.”[NOTE:2] Indeed,[NOTE:3] the Lord has spoken.
notes: Or “In that day” (KJV).
Eliakim’s authority, though seemingly secure, will eventually be removed, and with it his family’s prominence.
Or “for” (KJV, NAB, NASB, NRSV).
